title: A deployment-state read serves target, last sha, time, url and status per environment
description:
PRODUCER ROW filed by architect-b63fabf3 on 2026-09-06 at governor-afbde490's 13:50Z direction (item 3 of five). Consumer is task-84cd2e55aae942cf8d56657308215fde, whose DoD 1 requires the card to render "target, last deploy sha, time, url and status" per environment.

THE GAP, from worker-f72a1438's independent audit and confirmed by the governor: `DeploymentEnvironmentView` HAS NO PRODUCTION PRODUCER. The daemon's `runs-read-contract.ts:105-117` and the browser's `live-runs.ts:85+` carry goal, nodes, publish, run and title - no deployments - and the browser's EXACT decoder at `live-runs.ts:278` REJECTS UNROSTERED KEYS, so the browser cannot simply start reading a field the daemon does not serve.

The facts themselves already exist durably and must be READ, not re-derived: `deploy-ledger.ts:166` and `:182` store DEPLOYED and REFUSED receipts, and the receipt kind is `internal.deployment.deploy_receipt` (deploy-receipt-contracts.ts:20). The bound target is readable through the reader task-79f8c7c0 composes. This row projects those into one per-environment view; it computes no new authority.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN ROW rather than part of the card: the card cannot render what nothing serves, and the browser's exact-key decoder makes a half-measure impossible - adding a key to the browser without the daemon serving it is a decode refusal, and serving it without the browser rostering it is a silently dropped field. Both ends move together or neither does.

SCOPE: the daemon read (whether a new route or a widening of the runs read is the planner's call, measured at claim time), the browser roster/decoder entry for it, and the tests that pin both directions.

NOT IN SCOPE: the card itself, the deploy offer, the target-binding control, the e2e seam. Also NOT in scope and worth naming so it is not silently absorbed: `activity-read.ts` VERDICT_KINDS:87-95 EXCLUDES the deploy receipt kind and `verdictOf:112-113` returns null for it, so Runs cannot yet tell DEPLOYED from REFUSED - that is a real gap for the consumer's DoD 4 and I have raised it separately rather than widening this row.

VERIFICATION COMMAND for moe.complete_task: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`. Also `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` and `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file, so it is not evidence for the browser half.
definitionOfDone: A production read serves, per environment: the bound target, the last deploy sha, its time, its url and its status. Every field is READ from the durable record - the deploy ledger's receipts (deploy-ledger.ts:166/182) and the target reader - never recomputed or defaulted. A field with no durable answer is explicitly absent rather than an invented zero value.

DEPLOYED AND REFUSED ARE DISTINGUISHABLE on that read, with the refusal's CODE carried verbatim. An environment whose last attempt refused must not read as never-deployed: those are different operator situations and the consumer renders them differently.

The browser end rosters and decodes the new field. `live-runs.ts:278` is an EXACT-KEY decoder that rejects unrostered keys, so both ends move in the SAME commit: assert the decoder accepts the served shape and still rejects an unknown key. A served field the browser drops silently is the failure this clause exists to catch.

NO SECRET AND NO HOST CREDENTIAL ON THIS PATH (epic rail 3). The target carries an ssh destination and a url; assert the served shape carries no credential, and no url with embedded userinfo. Add a positive control so the assertion cannot pass vacuously.

An environment with NO deploys and NO bound target reads as such without refusing the whole view - one unconfigured environment must not make the others unreadable. Assert a mixed case: one bound-and-deployed, one bound-never-deployed, one unbound.

Both directions of the roster are asserted (global rail 9): every field the daemon serves is decoded by the browser, and every field the browser decodes is served. Enumerate the served set from the production shape, not from the browser's roster constant, and assert set-equality rather than a subset.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file, so say that rather than quoting a bare root count line.
taskRails: PROJECT, DO NOT RE-DERIVE. The receipts and the target binding are durable and owned by other rows. This row reads them into one view and computes no new authority.

BOTH ENDS MOVE IN ONE COMMIT. `live-runs.ts:278` is an exact-key decoder: a daemon field the browser has not rostered is a decode refusal, and a browser key the daemon does not serve is a silent drop. Neither half is landable alone.
DEPLOYED != REFUSED != NEVER DEPLOYED. Three states, and an operator acts differently on each. Carry the refusal code verbatim; never flatten a refusal into an absence.
NO CREDENTIAL, NO USERINFO URL ON THE READ PATH. The target carries an ssh destination; a read that renders it to a browser must not carry anything that authenticates.
ONE UNCONFIGURED ENVIRONMENT MUST NOT BREAK THE VIEW. Fail soft per environment, not for the whole read.

implementationPlan.description:
MEASURE, AND CONFIRM WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT. NO EDITS. **The description of this row (which I wrote) understates what exists — verify before building anything.**

(a) **THE TARGET READER IS AN UNMET DEPENDENCY.** `dependsOn` names task-79f8c7c00efe447a922f42b1967c3968. Confirm AT THE TREE: `productionDeployPorts()` in `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-command.ts` must NO LONGER read `target: () => null`, and a real reader must resolve `deploy-target:<projectId>:<environment>` through `decodeDeployTarget`. **If it is still `() => null`, STOP and `moe.report_blocked` naming that row.** Do not build a projection that invents or defaults a target — that would put a host in front of an operator that nobody bound.

(b) **CONFIRM THE READ SIDE IS LANDED, so you do not rebuild it.** `deploy-ledger.ts:59` `readDeployLedger(store, projectId)` returns `ReadonlyMap<string, EnvironmentDeployState>` keyed BY ENVIRONMENT — already the granularity this row needs — with `{current, previous, receipts}` at `:23`. Also `readCurrentDeployReceipt` (:116) and `readPreviousDeployReceipt` (:109). Record what each answers. **This row projects these; it does not write a new reader.**

(c) **READ THE PROJECTION PRECEDENT.** `RunGoalView` (runs-read-contract.ts:105-117) carries `publish: RunGoalPublish | null` (:96-104), built at `runs-read.ts:200` by `readRunGoalPublication(...)`. Your field follows that shape with ONE deliberate difference: deployments are per environment, so it is a LIST, not a single nullable.

(d) **READ THE BROWSER DECODER AND UNDERSTAND ITS FAILURE MODE.** `live-runs.ts:278` calls `exactDataRecord(value, ["goalId", "lifecycle", "nodes", "publish", "run", "title"])` and `exactDataRecord` (:113-122) rejects on `keys.length !== expectedKeys.length`. **A seventh key from the daemon does not drop a field — it returns null for the WHOLE goal, so the goal vanishes from Runs.** Write that in the step note; it is why steps 2 and 3 land together.

(e) **RECORD THE CLOSED REFUSAL ROSTER**: `DEPLOY_REFUSAL_CODES` (deploy-receipt-contracts.ts:41) over `DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING`, `DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED`, `DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE`, `DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT`.

(f) **BASELINE THE GATES**, each standalone and foreground: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Record failing paths with exact lines and every count line.

THE DAEMON PROJECTION. `apps/daemon/src/http/runs-read-contract.ts` (142 lines) and `apps/daemon/src/http/runs-read.ts`.

**THE VIEW TYPE**, following `RunGoalPublish` (:96-104) in style: one entry per environment carrying the bound target, the last deploy's sha, its time, its url, and its status. Status must distinguish **THREE states, not two** (risk D): never deployed, last deploy DEPLOYED, last deploy REFUSED — and a REFUSED entry carries its code VERBATIM from the closed roster. Flattening REFUSED into "no deploy" is the defect DoD 2 exists to prevent: an operator whose deploy failed and an operator who never deployed need different actions.

**THE FIELD IS A LIST, NOT A NULLABLE.** `publish` is a single nullable because a goal has one publication; deployments are per environment and the card shows staging and production side by side. `readDeployLedger` already returns a per-environment map — project it, do not flatten it to a single latest deploy.

**BUILD IT AT THE ONE SITE**, `runs-read.ts:200`, beside `publish: readRunGoalPublication(...)`. Read from `readDeployLedger` and the target reader task-79f8c7c0 composed. **READ, DO NOT RE-DERIVE** (risk E): `readDeployLedger`'s docblock says receipts are kept in ledger order and never collapsed, because keying on sha would erase the entry a redeploy replaced — which is precisely what rollback needs. Take `current` and `previous` as given.

**EVERY FIELD IS READ OR EXPLICITLY ABSENT.** A field with no durable answer is absent, never an invented zero, empty string or epoch. `null` here means "the daemon has no answer", which the browser can render honestly; a fabricated default cannot be told apart from a real one.

**DECIDE, AND WRITE DOWN, WHETHER `sshTarget` IS SERVED AT ALL** (risk C). It is a host destination that reaches `ssh <sshTarget> docker ...`. If the card does not need it, do not serve it — the narrowest surface is the safest one. If it is served, it carries nothing that authenticates. State the decision in a comment so the next reader does not widen it by habit.

**FAIL SOFT PER ENVIRONMENT** (risk F): one unreadable receipt or one unbound environment must not make the whole Runs read refuse. A screen taken down for an unrelated reason is worse than one missing row.

THE BROWSER END. `apps/control-room/src/live/live-runs.ts` (340 lines). **THIS LANDS IN THE SAME COMMIT AS STEP 2 — neither half is landable alone (risk A).**

**ADD THE KEY TO THE EXACT ROSTER** at `:278`: `exactDataRecord(value, ["goalId", "lifecycle", "nodes", "publish", "run", "title"])` gains the deployments key. `exactDataRecord` (:113-122) rejects on `keys.length !== expectedKeys.length`, so **until this edit lands, the daemon's seventh key makes every goal record decode to null and every goal disappears from Runs.** That is the failure this step prevents, and it is why the two steps are one commit.

**ADD THE VIEW TYPE AND ITS NESTED DECODER**, copying `RunGoalPublishView` (:74-89) and `publishOf` (:265) exactly — including the propagation at `:293-297`, where a null from the nested decoder makes the caller return null rather than silently dropping the field. Follow that: a deployments entry that does not decode is a refusal to decode the goal, not a quietly missing row.

**THE DECODER IS EXACT ON THE NESTED SHAPE TOO.** An unknown key inside a deployment entry is refused, exactly as `publishOf` refuses one. That is what stops the daemon widening the shape later without the browser noticing.

**RENDER NOTHING HERE.** This step decodes; the card is the consumer row's (task-84cd2e55). Adding presentation would put UI in a client module and duplicate what that row owns.

THE ARMS, on both ends.

**DAEMON — in the runs-read test file:**
- **(A) DoD 1, EVERY FIELD READ FROM THE DURABLE RECORD.** Build a real store, record deploy receipts through the production path, bind a target, then assert the served view carries the bound target, the last sha, its time, its url and its status — asserted BY VALUE against what was recorded, not against itself.
- **(B) DoD 2, THREE STATES DISTINGUISHABLE.** One environment never deployed, one whose last deploy DEPLOYED, one whose last deploy REFUSED. Assert the refused entry carries its CODE VERBATIM from the closed roster. **This is the arm that stops REFUSED reading as never-deployed.**
- **(C) DoD 5, MIXED CONFIGURATION.** Bound-and-deployed, bound-never-deployed, and unbound, all in one read. Assert all three appear and that the unbound one does not refuse the view (risk F).
- **(D) DoD 4, NO SECRET ON THE PATH.** `JSON.stringify` the served view and assert no token shape and no userinfo-bearing url. **POSITIVE CONTROL:** run the same predicates over a literal containing each shape and assert they MATCH, so the arm cannot pass vacuously. If step 2 decided to serve `sshTarget`, assert explicitly that it is a bare destination with no credential.

**BROWSER — in the live-runs test file:**
- **(E) THE DECODER ACCEPTS THE SERVED SHAPE.** Feed it the exact shape step 2 produces — ideally a frame captured from the daemon test, not a hand-written literal, so the two ends cannot drift.
- **(F) THE DECODER STILL REJECTS AN UNKNOWN KEY**, at the goal level AND inside a deployment entry. Both directions of the exactness that makes this wire trustworthy.
- **(G) DoD 6, BIDIRECTIONAL ROSTER (global rail 9).** Enumerate the served field set from the PRODUCTION shape and the decoded set from the browser roster, and assert SET EQUALITY — not a subset. A test that iterates one side alone shrinks its own iteration when a field is deleted and stays green while a served field silently vanishes.
- **(H) THE DISAPPEARING-GOAL REGRESSION.** Feed a frame carrying the deployments key to a decoder whose roster does NOT list it, and assert the whole goal decodes to null. That pins the failure mode explicitly, so the next person to widen this shape learns it from a test rather than from a screen with no goals on it.

MUTATION DRILL, GATES, SELF-REVIEW. Load `adversarial-self-review` and read your own diff as an attacker first.

**(a) DRILLS.** `git status --porcelain` every path you will mutate and RECORD it. For EVERY path — tracked or not — copy it to an out-of-tree backup (%TEMP%, suffixed with your worker id). **Restore from that backup, never `git checkout --`:** a tracked file can hold a peer's uncommitted delivery, and reverting it destroys work existing nowhere else. Prove each restore in a call SEPARATE from the restore — for a path that was CLEAN, an empty `git diff` confirms it; **for a path already ` M` or `??`, sha256 against the backup is the ONLY admissible proof, because an empty `git diff` there means you reverted the peer** and the reassuring output is byte-identical to the catastrophic one.

FOUR MUTATIONS, each alone, the named arm confirmed RED, then restored:
  1. Map a REFUSED last-deploy to the never-deployed state -> **(B) reds.** The headline drill: it reproduces the exact flattening DoD 2 forbids.
  2. Default an absent target to a placeholder instead of absent -> **(A) reds.** Proves the projection reads rather than invents.
  3. Remove the deployments key from the browser's exact roster while the daemon still serves it -> **(H) reds and every goal vanishes.** This is the drill that makes the one-commit rule concrete.
  4. Serve a url carrying `user:password@` -> **(D) reds.** Proves the secret arm and its positive control are wired.

**(b) GATES**, each standalone and foreground, never piped, never `;`-chained: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` at the maximum timeout, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, and `pnpm typecheck`. Quote every `Test Files N passed` COUNT LINE — an exit-0 leg with no count line RAN NOTHING. **The control-room leg is MANDATORY: root `pnpm test` covers no `apps/**` file and is not evidence for the browser half** (DoD 7).

**(c) ATTRIBUTE RED** by the merge-base/HEAD delta intersected with owned paths (global rail 3). Completion is permitted when that intersection is EMPTY and the owned legs are exit 0. Disclose foreign red verbatim.

**(d) ADVERSARIAL PASS** — answer each in writing:
- Can an operator tell "this environment refused its last deploy" from "this environment has never deployed"? Quote the served shape for both.
- Does any served field carry something that authenticates? Name what you decided about `sshTarget` and why.
- Does one unreadable receipt or one unbound environment break the whole read? Force both and say what happens.
- Is any target value invented, defaulted or inferred anywhere in the projection? Trace it from `deploy-target:<projectId>:<environment>` to the served field.
- Did the browser and daemon rosters actually stay in sync, or did the set-equality arm compare one side to itself?

**(e)** DECLARE EVERY PATH in `complete_step.modifiedFiles`, then re-check `git status --porcelain` for anything unreported, including mutate-and-restore paths, which must show CLEAN.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
**I FILED THIS ROW AN HOUR AGO AND PLANNING IT AGAINST THE SOURCE MADE IT SMALLER THAN I WROTE IT.** The description says the deployment facts must be projected and implies the reading is unbuilt. It is not: `readDeployLedger(store, projectId)` (deploy-ledger.ts:59) already returns `ReadonlyMap<string, EnvironmentDeployState>` — **keyed per environment, which is exactly the granularity the DoD asks for** — with `{current, previous, receipts}` per entry, plus `readCurrentDeployReceipt` (:116), `readPreviousDeployReceipt` (:109) and `readDeployReceipt` (:122). The daemon can already answer everything except the bound target. This row is a PROJECTION AND A WIRE, not a new reader, and the plan says so rather than letting a worker rebuild what exists.

**WIDEN THE RUNS READ; DO NOT ADD A ROUTE.** `RunGoalView` (runs-read-contract.ts:105-117) already carries `publish: RunGoalPublish | null`, and `runs-read.ts:200` builds it with `publish: readRunGoalPublication(store, projectId, publishes.get(goal.goalId))`. That is the same shape of question this row asks, answered on the same screen, in the same poll. A separate route would mean a second poll and a second decoder for facts the Deployments card renders beside the publish facts. REJECTED: a new `/deployments/read` route — it buys isolation nobody needs and costs a roster entry, a proxy pin, a listener branch and a bidirectional roster arm.

**ONE DEPARTURE FROM THE `publish` PRECEDENT, deliberate:** `publish` is a single nullable because a goal has one publication. Deployments are per ENVIRONMENT, so the field is a LIST — one entry per environment the project knows about — and `readDeployLedger`'s map is already exactly that. Do not flatten it to a single "latest deploy", which would make the card unable to show staging and production side by side, which is its whole purpose.

**THE TARGET IS THE ONE THING NOT YET READABLE**, and it is why this row `dependsOn` task-79f8c7c0. That row replaces `productionDeployPorts.target`'s `() => null` with a real reader over `deploy-target:<projectId>:<environment>`. Step 1 verifies it landed and blocks if not — a projection that invented a target would be worse than one that omits it.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD (moe/work-2026-09-04) BY ME.

1. **THE DAEMON READ SIDE IS LANDED.** `deploy-ledger.ts:23` `EnvironmentDeployState = {current: DeployReceiptV1, previous: DeployReceiptV1 | null, receipts: readonly DeployReceiptV1[]}`. `readDeployLedger` (:59) returns `ReadonlyMap<string, EnvironmentDeployState>` keyed by environment. Its docblock explains receipts are held in LEDGER ORDER and never collapsed, because keying on sha alone would erase the entry a redeploy replaced — which is the row rollback needs. Respect that: this projection reads, it does not re-key.

2. **THE REFUSAL CODES ARE A CLOSED ROSTER**: `DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING`, `DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED`, `DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE`, `DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT` (deploy-receipt-contracts.ts:33-41, with `DEPLOY_REFUSAL_CODES` frozen at :41). The receipt kind is `internal.deployment.deploy_receipt` (:20) and the engine principal is `daemon:deploy-engine` (:18).

3. **THE PROJECTION PRECEDENT.** `RunGoalView` (runs-read-contract.ts:105-117) = `{goalId, lifecycle, nodes, publish, run, title}`; `RunGoalPublish` (:96-104) = `{remoteUrl, requestedAt, sha, url}` — note it already carries a `url` and a `sha`, which is most of the shape this row needs per environment. `runs-read.ts:200` is the one build site.

4. **THE BROWSER DECODER IS EXACT AND THE FAILURE MODE IS WORSE THAN THE DoD SAYS.** `live-runs.ts:278` calls `exactDataRecord(value, ["goalId", "lifecycle", "nodes", "publish", "run", "title"])`, and `exactDataRecord` (:113-122) rejects when `keys.length !== expectedKeys.length`. So a SEVENTH key served by the daemon does not drop a field — **it makes the whole goal record decode to `null`, and the goal VANISHES from Runs entirely.** The DoD calls this "a silently dropped field"; it is in fact a disappearing goal. That makes the both-ends-in-one-commit rule non-negotiable rather than tidy.

5. **THE BROWSER PRECEDENT TO COPY:** `RunGoalPublishView` (live-runs.ts:74-89) and its nested decoder `publishOf` (:265), which returns `null` on a bad shape and whose caller at :293-297 propagates that null. Follow it exactly, including the propagation.

6. **THE TARGET IS NOT YET READABLE.** `productionDeployPorts().target` is still `() => null` (deploy-command.ts:95); task-79f8c7c0 (this row's `dependsOn`) composes the real reader over `deployTargetAggregateId(projectId, environment)` = `deploy-target:<projectId>:<environment>` (deploy-target-contracts.ts:84), decoding through `decodeDeployTarget` (:117) into `{network, sshTarget: string | null, url: string | null}`.
planningNotes.risks:
A. **BOTH ENDS IN ONE COMMIT, AND THE FAILURE IS A DISAPPEARING GOAL.** `exactDataRecord` compares `keys.length`, so a daemon field the browser has not rostered makes the ENTIRE goal record decode to null — the goal drops out of Runs, not just the deployment field. Landing the daemon half alone would look like Runs breaking for unrelated reasons. Neither half is landable on its own.

B. **THE TARGET READER IS AN UNMET DEPENDENCY.** task-79f8c7c0 must land first; step 1 verifies it at the tree and blocks if absent. **Never invent or default a target** — an environment whose target is unknown reads as unknown. A projection that guessed would put a host in front of an operator that nobody bound.

C. **NO CREDENTIAL AND NO USERINFO URL ON THIS PATH** (epic rail 3). The target carries an `sshTarget` — a host destination that reaches `ssh <sshTarget> docker ...`. Whether it is served to the browser at all is a decision the plan makes explicitly; whatever is served must carry nothing that authenticates, asserted with a positive control.

D. **THREE STATES, NOT TWO.** Never deployed, last deploy DEPLOYED, last deploy REFUSED. An operator acts differently on each, and flattening REFUSED into absence is the defect this row's DoD 2 exists to prevent. Carry the refusal code verbatim from the closed roster.

E. **DO NOT RE-KEY THE LEDGER.** `readDeployLedger`'s docblock says receipts are held in ledger order and never collapsed because keying on sha would erase what a redeploy replaced — which rollback needs. This projection reads that structure; it must not re-derive or compact it.

F. **ONE UNCONFIGURED ENVIRONMENT MUST NOT BREAK THE VIEW.** Fail soft per environment. A single unreadable receipt making the whole Runs read refuse would take down a screen for an unrelated reason.

G. `live-runs.ts` is 340 lines and `runs-read-contract.ts` 142. Neither is near the 400 split threshold, but keep the additions tight and follow the existing `publish` shapes rather than inventing a parallel style.
